pharm: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist; enhances glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppresses glucagon, and slows gastric emptying
quick: SC: 0.25 mg weekly x4 wk, then titrate to 0.5-2 mg weekly. Oral (Rybelsus): 3 mg daily x30 days, then 7-14 mg daily
SC: any time, with or without food. Oral Rybelsus: empty stomach with <=4 oz water, wait >=30 min before food/drink/other meds
Not recommended; discontinue >=2 months before planned pregnancy
No dose adjustment; monitor renal function if volume depletion from GI effects
No specific restriction; watch hypoglycemia with insulin/secretagogues
HbA1c, glucose, renal function, MTC symptoms, retinopathy in at-risk patients
summary: Semaglutide is a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist used as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus, and to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events in those at high cardiovascular risk. It lowers glucose in a glucose-dependent manner by stimulating insulin and suppressing glucagon secretion, and delays gastric emptying. It is available as a once-weekly subcutaneous injection (Ozempic) and as a once-daily oral tablet (Rybelsus). It carries a boxed warning for the risk of thyroid C-cell tumors observed in rodents and is contraindicated in patients with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or with Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2.
indications: As an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus

To reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke) in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus and established cardiovascular disease or high cardiovascular risk

dosage.d: Start 0.25 mg once weekly for 4 weeks; then increase to 0.5 mg once weekly; if additional control needed after >=4 weeks, increase to 1 mg, then to maximum 2 mg once weekly
dosage.t: Once weekly, any time of day, with or without food; rotate injection sites (abdomen, thigh, upper arm)
dosage.n: The 0.25 mg dose is for initiation and is not effective for glycemic control

dosage.d: Start 3 mg once daily for 30 days; then increase to 7 mg once daily; if additional control needed after >=30 days, may increase to maximum 14 mg once daily
dosage.t: On an empty stomach in the morning with up to 4 oz (120 mL) water; wait at least 30 minutes before eating, drinking, or other oral medications
dosage.n: The 3 mg dose is for initiation and is not effective for glycemic control; swallow whole, do not split, crush, or chew

dosage.d: Oral 14 mg daily approximates SC 0.5 mg weekly; there is no equivalent oral dose for SC 1 mg or 2 mg weekly
dosage.n: Patients on Rybelsus 7 mg may transition to Ozempic 0.5 mg SC weekly the day after the last oral dose

admin: Subcutaneous: inject into the abdomen, thigh, or upper arm and rotate injection sites; do not inject into the same site repeatedly
Subcutaneous: administer once weekly on the same day; the dosing day may be changed if at least 48 hours separate two doses
Oral (Rybelsus): take first thing in the morning on an empty stomach with no more than 4 ounces of plain water
Oral: swallow the tablet whole; do not split, crush, chew, or dissolve; wait at least 30 minutes before food, other beverages, or oral medications
Inspect injectable solution; it should be clear and colorless. Do not use if particulate matter or discoloration is present
moa: Semaglutide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist that selectively binds to and activates the GLP-1 receptor, the target for native GLP-1. It increases insulin secretion and lowers glucagon secretion, both in a glucose-dependent manner, so that insulin secretion is stimulated and glucagon secretion is suppressed when blood glucose is high. It also causes a minor delay in gastric emptying in the early postprandial phase. These actions together lower fasting and postprandial glucose. The glucose-dependent mechanism limits the risk of hypoglycemia when used alone.

absolute: Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC)
Prior serious hypersensitivity reaction to semaglutide or any excipient
relative: Diabetic retinopathy (risk of temporary worsening with rapid glucose improvement)
Concomitant insulin or insulin secretagogues (hypoglycemia risk)
monitor: Symptoms of medullary thyroid carcinoma (neck mass, dysphagia, dyspnea, persistent hoarseness)
Renal function during significant GI adverse reactions
Diabetic retinopathy progression in at-risk patients

preg: Available data are insufficient to evaluate for a drug-associated risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or other adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. Animal reproduction studies showed embryofetal mortality, structural abnormalities, and alterations to growth at maternal exposures below the maximum recommended human dose. Because of the long half-life, semaglutide should be discontinued in women at least 2 months before a planned pregnancy. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: There are no data on the presence of semaglutide in human milk or its effects on the breastfed infant or on milk production. For the oral formulation, metabolites of the absorption enhancer SNAC are present in milk and higher plasma levels may occur in neonates and infants. Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment with semaglutide.
renal: No dosage adjustment is recommended in patients with renal impairment, including end-stage renal disease; the recommended dosage is the same as for patients with normal renal function. Monitor renal function when initiating or escalating in patients who report severe gastrointestinal adverse reactions that could lead to volume depletion and acute kidney injury.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is recommended in patients with hepatic impairment. The recommended dosage is the same as for patients with normal hepatic function.

major: Insulin and insulin secretagogues such as sulfonylureas (increased risk of hypoglycemia, including severe hypoglycemia; reduce dose of the concomitant agent)
moderate: Oral medications in general (delayed gastric emptying may alter absorption; monitor narrow therapeutic index drugs)
Levothyroxine (exposure increased approximately 33% with oral semaglutide; monitor thyroid function)
minor: No clinically significant changes seen with metformin, digoxin, oral contraceptives, or warfarin in interaction studies
interactions.food: Subcutaneous form may be taken with or without food. Oral Rybelsus must be taken on an empty stomach with limited water and a 30-minute fasting window afterward, as food markedly reduces absorption
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; counsel on hypoglycemia risk if combined with insulin or secretagogues
interactions.diagnostics: Routine monitoring of serum calcitonin or thyroid ultrasound is of uncertain value for early detection of MTC; counsel on symptoms instead

rare: Thyroid C-cell tumors / medullary thyroid carcinoma (rodent finding; human risk unknown)
Pulmonary aspiration during anesthesia or deep sedation
emergency: Anaphylaxis or angioedema - stop drug and seek emergency care
Severe persistent abdominal pain radiating to the back (possible pancreatitis) - seek urgent evaluation
Severe hypoglycemia with confusion or loss of consciousness

monitoring: HbA1c every 3 to 6 months and fasting/postprandial glucose
Renal function, particularly during dose escalation or significant GI losses
Signs and symptoms of pancreatitis and gallbladder disease
Diabetic retinopathy status in patients with a history of retinopathy
Symptoms suggestive of thyroid tumors (neck mass, dysphagia, dyspnea, persistent hoarseness)
counsel: Report symptoms of a thyroid tumor such as a lump in the neck, trouble swallowing, shortness of breath, or persistent hoarseness
Seek care for severe ongoing abdominal pain that may radiate to the back, which can signal pancreatitis
Nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea are most common during dose escalation and usually improve; stay hydrated
For Rybelsus, take on an empty stomach with no more than 4 ounces of water and wait at least 30 minutes before food, drink, or other medicines
Inform anesthesia and surgical teams that you take semaglutide before any procedure requiring sedation; discuss stopping at least 2 months before a planned pregnancy
pk: Glucose-lowering begins within days; steady state reached after 4 to 5 weeks of regular dosing
Subcutaneous: 1 to 3 days post-injection; oral: approximately 1 hour after dosing
Present in the circulation for about 5 weeks after the last dose
Unused pens refrigerated 2-8 C (36-46 F); after first use store per labeling at room temperature or refrigerated; do not freeze; protect from light. Rybelsus tablets at 20-25 C (68-77 F)
pearls: Once-weekly subcutaneous dosing improves adherence; oral Rybelsus offers a non-injectable option with strict empty-stomach administration
The lowest doses (SC 0.25 mg, oral 3 mg) are for initiation only and are not effective for glycemic control
Glucose-dependent action means low intrinsic hypoglycemia risk unless combined with insulin or sulfonylureas
Demonstrated cardiovascular benefit in type 2 diabetes with established cardiovascular disease
Long half-life means effects and the need for contraception planning persist for weeks after stopping
missed: Subcutaneous: administer the missed dose as soon as possible within 5 days; if more than 5 days have passed, skip it and resume the regular weekly schedule. Oral (Rybelsus): skip the missed dose and take the next dose the following day; do not take two tablets together.
overdose: Overdose may produce severe nausea, vomiting, and hypoglycemia (especially with insulin or secretagogues). There is no specific antidote. Initiate appropriate supportive treatment guided by clinical signs and symptoms, and provide an extended observation and treatment period given the approximately 1-week half-life. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
